project.name: sousvide
project.description: SOUS VIDE (Scene Understanding via Synthesized Visual Inertial Data from Experts) - a Stanford MSL research project for training and deploying learned drone flight-control policies using synthesized data from Gaussian-splat simulation (FiGS).

nodes.name: network_factory.py
nodes.summary: Factory that instantiates or loads a neural network module for a pilot based on a configuration dictionary, dispatching to the correct network class (BaseNet, DINO, SIFU, SVNet, DNNet, Pave) by network_type and caching results as .pt files on disk.

nodes.name: generate_network
nodes.summary: Loads a pilot's saved network checkpoint if one exists on disk, otherwise constructs a new network instance of the requested type (simple, dino, sifu, svnet, dnnet, pave) from its configuration dictionary.

nodes.name: network_helper.py
nodes.summary: Utility module providing input/output index resolution, dimension/size computation, tensor extraction, and sinusoidal positional encoding generation shared across all SousVide network architectures.

nodes.name: get_max_length
nodes.summary: Computes the maximum sequence length across sequence-type input/output index groups.

nodes.name: get_io_refr
nodes.summary: Loads a reference dictionary of input/output field definitions (basic, sequence, or image) from a JSON config file located relative to the module path.

nodes.name: get_io_dims
nodes.summary: Computes the dimensionality (element count) for each named input/output index group.

nodes.name: get_io_sizes
nodes.summary: Computes the flattened total size (product of dimensions) for each named input/output index group by delegating to get_io_dims.

nodes.name: get_io_idxs
nodes.summary: Resolves a network's input/output configuration entries into concrete tensor index lists, handling basic, sequence, and image reference types with validation.

nodes.name: extract_io
nodes.summary: Extracts named input/output tensor slices from a source dictionary of tensors using precomputed index mappings, for feeding into a network's forward pass.

nodes.name: generate_positional_encoding
nodes.summary: Generates a standard sinusoidal transformer-style positional encoding tensor for a given model dimension and maximum sequence length.

nodes.name: base_net.py
nodes.summary: Defines BaseNet, an abstract PyTorch nn.Module base class that normalizes input/output configs into prediction/deployment index maps and provides shared dimension/size helpers, which all SousVide network architectures subclass.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Python's ABC/abstractmethod alongside nn.Module for a dual-inheritance abstract PyTorch base class.

nodes.name: BaseNet
nodes.summary: Abstract base class for all SousVide network types; normalizes prediction/deployment input-output configs, computes history length (Nhy), and exposes get_io_dims/get_io_sizes helpers while leaving forward() to subclasses.

nodes.name: dnnet.py
nodes.summary: Defines DNNet, a SousVide command network subclass that fuses image features (via a small CNN), a heatmap channel, and history features through an MLP head to output a control command vector.

nodes.name: DNNet
nodes.summary: Command network combining a convolutional image branch with an MLP over concatenated image/state/history features to predict flight control commands.

nodes.name: feature_extractors.py
nodes.summary: Defines vision transformer feature extractor networks: VitB16 (a torchvision ViT-B/16 wrapper exposing patch/class tokens) and DINO (a BaseNet subclass wrapping a pretrained DINOv2 model for image feature extraction).
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps HuggingFace transformers' AutoModel alongside torchvision's ViT implementation for two different pretrained backbones.

nodes.name: VitB16
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around torchvision's ViT-B/16 model that manually runs the patch embedding, class token concatenation, and encoder to return patch tokens and the class token separately.

nodes.name: DINO
nodes.summary: BaseNet subclass loading a pretrained DINOv2 transformer to extract patch and class-token image features for downstream SousVide networks.

nodes.name: pave.py
nodes.summary: Defines Pave, a SousVide command network with separate actor and critic MLP heads that outputs a stochastic control action (sampled from a Normal distribution with log-probability) plus a critic value estimate.

nodes.name: Pave
nodes.summary: Actor-critic command network producing a sampled control action with log-probability (actor) and a state-value estimate (critic) for reinforcement-learning-style policy training.

nodes.name: sifu.py
nodes.summary: Defines SIFU (Sequence Into Features Unified), a feedforward MLP network that maps history sequences to estimated drone parameters (mass, thrust coefficient) during training and outputs a penultimate-layer feature vector at deployment.

nodes.name: SIFU
nodes.summary: MLP-based history encoder that estimates physical drone parameters during training and serves as a reusable feature extractor at runtime.

nodes.name: svnet.py
nodes.summary: Defines SVNet, the original SousVide command network combining a SqueezeNet image backbone with two MLP branches over state and history features, concatenated to produce a control command.

nodes.name: SVNet
nodes.summary: Command network fusing SqueezeNet-derived image features with state and history MLP branches via concatenation to output a flight control command.

nodes.name: policy.py
nodes.summary: Defines Policy, the top-level learned control policy module that assembles and chains multiple sub-networks (e.g. featNet, commNet) generated via network_factory into a single forward pass producing the flight command output.

nodes.name: Policy
nodes.summary: Top-level nn.Module that builds a named collection of sub-networks from a policy configuration and chains their forward passes, threading intermediate outputs (features, patches, class tokens) into the final control command.

nodes.name: flight_helper.py
nodes.summary: Computes per-flight performance metrics (tracking error and post-processing inference time statistics) from recorded trajectory rollouts, used to evaluate deployed policies.

nodes.name: compute_flight_metrics
nodes.summary: Computes per-trajectory tracking error (TTE) and post-processing inference time statistics from a list of trajectory rollouts, applying a threshold to filter valid points.

nodes.name: plot_3D.py
nodes.summary: Provides 3D matplotlib plotting utilities for visualizing drone flight trajectories, waypoints, and quadrotor pose frames.

nodes.name: tXU_to_3D
nodes.summary: Renders a 3D plot of one or more state/control trajectories alongside waypoints and a desired trajectory, drawing quadrotor body frames at intervals.

nodes.name: RO_to_3D
nodes.summary: Converts raw rollout data (RO) into a tXU trajectory list and delegates to tXU_to_3D to render the 3D visualization.

nodes.name: plot_learning.py
nodes.summary: Plots training loss curves for student policy networks and visualizes deployment flight results, combining rich console summaries with matplotlib figures.

nodes.name: plot_losses
nodes.summary: Loads and aggregates training/testing loss histories for a cohort's student networks, prints a rich summary table, and plots per-student and combined loss curves.

nodes.name: plot_deployments
nodes.summary: Loads deployment trajectory data for a course/cohort, computes flight metrics per pilot, prints a summary table, and renders 3D trajectory plots.

nodes.name: plot_synthesize.py
nodes.summary: Visualizes synthesized rollout datasets for a training cohort, sampling and rendering 3D trajectories and time-domain plots alongside dataset descriptions.

nodes.name: plot_rollout_data
nodes.summary: Samples and visualizes synthesized rollout datasets for a cohort, printing dataset descriptions and optionally showing 3D and time-domain plots for a randomly selected sample.

nodes.name: plot_time.py
nodes.summary: Provides time-series matplotlib plotting utilities for visualizing state and control trajectories over the flight horizon.

nodes.name: tXU_to_time
nodes.summary: Plots state and control trajectories over time in a grid of subplots, optionally overlaying a desired trajectory for comparison.

nodes.name: RO_to_time
nodes.summary: Converts raw rollout data (RO) into a tXU trajectory list and delegates to tXU_to_time to render the time-domain visualization.

nodes.name: plot_utilities.py
nodes.summary: Shared helper functions for the visualization module, computing plot axis limits and drawing quadrotor body-frame geometry for 3D plots.

nodes.name: get_plot_limits
nodes.summary: Computes symmetric or bounded axis limits for plotting given position data, with optional minimum, maximum, and absolute-max constraints.

nodes.name: quad_frame
nodes.summary: Draws a quadrotor's body-frame axes on a 3D matplotlib plot given a pose state vector containing position and orientation quaternion.

nodes.name: rich_utilities.py
nodes.summary: Rich-library console UI helpers shared across the project, providing progress bars for data generation and training, plus formatted tables and summaries for deployment and student training results.

nodes.name: get_generation_progress
nodes.summary: Builds a Rich Progress bar configured with columns suited for tracking data generation tasks.

nodes.name: get_training_progress
nodes.summary: Builds a Rich Progress bar with a spinner and columns configured for tracking training tasks.

nodes.name: get_data_description
nodes.summary: Formats a labeled, padded description string for a named dataset value with its subunit label, used in dataset summary output.

nodes.name: get_deployment_table
nodes.summary: Constructs a Rich Table pre-configured with columns for reporting per-pilot flight deployment metrics.

nodes.name: update_deployment_table
nodes.summary: Adds a formatted row of computed flight metrics for a given pilot into a deployment results table.

nodes.name: get_student_summary
nodes.summary: Builds a formatted multi-metric summary string of a student network's training progress, including episode counts, data counts, losses, and evaluation error.

nodes.name: deploy_figs.py
nodes.summary: Orchestrates roster-level closed-loop deployment of trained pilots in the FiGS simulator, generating trajectories, running the simulation loop for each configuration/course/pilot combination, computing flight metrics, and saving deployment results and videos.

nodes.name: deploy_roster
nodes.summary: Main deployment loop that loads configs and gsplat scenes, builds desired trajectories via MinTimeSnap, runs the FiGS Simulator with a VehicleRateMPC or Pilot controller across courses and pilots, computes flight metrics, and reports progress via a rich table.

nodes.name: save_deployments
nodes.summary: Persists deployment trajectory/image data to disk as torch tensors and renders the recorded and desired flight trajectories as MP4 videos.

nodes.name: data_compress_helper.py
nodes.summary: Helper utilities to compress camera image stacks to JPEG bytes for compact storage and decompress them back into numpy arrays for training/analysis.

nodes.name: decompress_data
nodes.summary: Decompresses a dictionary of JPEG-encoded byte images back into stacked numpy image arrays for downstream use.

nodes.name: compress_data
nodes.summary: Encodes raw image arrays into JPEG byte buffers to reduce the size of saved rollout data files.

nodes.name: rollout_generator.py
nodes.summary: Generates synthetic rollout training data by simulating an expert (VehicleRateMPC) controller over perturbed frames and trajectory batches in FiGS, then saves the resulting trajectories and images (optionally compressed) for downstream policy training.

nodes.name: generate_rollout_data
nodes.summary: Top-level pipeline that loads configs and gsplat data per course, computes desired trajectories, sets up the simulator and expert MPC controller, batches timestamp splits, generates perturbed frames, and drives generate_rollouts/save_rollouts with progress reporting.

nodes.name: generate_rollouts
nodes.summary: Runs the simulation loop for a batch of perturbed initial frames, stepping the simulator/controller pair and collecting trajectory and image data for each viable rollout while filtering out failed or divergent runs.

nodes.name: save_rollouts
nodes.summary: Writes generated trajectory and image stacks to disk as torch .pt files under the course's data directory, optionally compressing images first.

nodes.name: synthesize_helper.py
nodes.summary: Collection of pure helper functions for synthetic data generation: randomized camera frame sampling, initial-state perturbations, batching of time-split points for rollouts, and patch-index/bounds computation for image cropping.

nodes.name: generate_frames
nodes.summary: Randomly samples camera frame parameter variations within specified bounds to produce a set of perturbed frame configurations for data diversity.

nodes.name: generate_perturbations
nodes.summary: Generates randomized initial-state perturbations (position, velocity, orientation) around a desired trajectory using obedient quaternion sampling, for training data diversity.

nodes.name: compute_Tsp_batches
nodes.summary: Computes randomized, optionally shuffled batches of trajectory timestamp splits used to schedule rollout segments across a desired flight duration.

nodes.name: get_patch_index
nodes.summary: Maps normalized image coordinates (u, v) to a row/column patch index within a gridded image layout.

nodes.name: get_patch_bounds
nodes.summary: Computes the pixel bounding box of the image patch corresponding to given normalized coordinates, using get_patch_index for grid lookup.

nodes.name: sousvide_utilities.py
nodes.summary: Shared numerical utilities for computing frame body-rate parameters, relative state/rotation weights (Wrs) between simulated rollouts and the objective frame, and formatted flight-output (FOro) arrays used across deployment and rollout generation.

nodes.name: compute_prms
nodes.summary: Computes parameter values from a frame configuration, used as inputs elsewhere in the flight/rollout pipeline.

nodes.name: compute_Wrs
nodes.summary: Computes relative state and rotation-weighted values between rollout trajectories (Xro, Uro, Wro) and a reference/body frame, used to express dynamics data in the frame's coordinate system.

nodes.name: compute_FOro
nodes.summary: Assembles time, state, input, and weight rollout data into a combined flight-output (FOro) array format used for saving and downstream training.

nodes.name: record_flight.py
nodes.summary: Defines FlightRecorder, a class that records state, input, and camera image data at each simulation timestep during a flight, applies image preprocessing transforms, and saves the recorded flight data and rendered video to disk.

nodes.name: FlightRecorder
nodes.summary: Records per-timestep flight state, control input, and camera images during a simulated flight, applies an albumentations preprocessing pipeline to images, and saves the resulting flight log (states, inputs, images) plus an MP4 video to the pilot's data directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the albumentations library (Compose/Resize/CenterCrop/Normalize/ToTensorV2) to build an image transform pipeline applied per-frame during recording.

nodes.name: pilot.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Pilot class, a BaseController subclass implementing the OODA (Observe-Retain-Collate-Act, i.e. ORCA) loop that feeds sensor observations (state, RGB image, force/torque) through a Policy neural network to produce control commands for drone flight, while maintaining rolling history buffers for sequence models.
nodes.languageNotes: Maintains GPU tensor buffers for current/previous state and a rolling sequence history dict (Sqc) indexed circularly via sqc_idx, avoiding reallocation on every timestep for real-time control.

nodes.name: Pilot
nodes.summary: Runtime controller that wraps a Policy network, managing device placement, image preprocessing, sequence-history buffers, and the observe/retain/collate/act control cycle used both for live deployment (ORCA) and training-time inference.

nodes.name: losses.py
nodes.summary: Provides loss function utilities for training policy networks: entropy and load-balance regularizers for mixture-of-experts gating weights, and a LossFn class computing summed MSE loss across multiple prediction/label keys.

nodes.name: loss_entropy
nodes.summary: Computes the negative mean entropy of a weights tensor, used as a regularization term to encourage diverse gating in mixture-of-experts style networks.

nodes.name: loss_load_balance
nodes.summary: Computes the variance of mean gating weights across the batch, penalizing imbalanced expert utilization in mixture-of-experts training.

nodes.name: LossFn
nodes.summary: Callable loss wrapper that sums mean-squared-error losses across all matching keys between predicted and label dictionaries, used as the training criterion for the policy network.

nodes.name: synthesized_data.py
nodes.summary: Provides the ObservationData PyTorch Dataset wrapping synthesized observation tensors, plus helpers to load a dataset from a .pt file and to enumerate train/test observation data file paths for a given cohort, student, and topic.

nodes.name: ObservationData
nodes.summary: PyTorch Dataset that stores squeezed input/output observation tensors (possibly nested in lists/dicts) and exposes them by index for use with a DataLoader during policy training.

nodes.name: squeeze_data
nodes.summary: Recursively squeezes the batch dimension out of tensors nested arbitrarily within lists and dicts, normalizing observation data shapes for dataset storage.

nodes.name: generate_dataset
nodes.summary: Loads a topic's serialized observation tensors from disk onto the target device and wraps them into an ObservationData Dataset instance.

nodes.name: get_data_paths
nodes.summary: Scans the cohort's observation_data directory tree to build train and test file path lists per course, holding out the last file of each course for testing (or reusing the single file when only one exists).

nodes.name: train_policy.py
nodes.summary: Orchestrates supervised training of student policy networks: regenerates observation data if requested, runs per-student training loops with checkpointing, periodic in-training flight evaluation via deploy_figs, best-checkpoint selection, and rich progress reporting.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses contextlib.redirect_stdout with an io.StringIO buffer to silence noisy deploy_roster output during periodic in-training evaluation.

nodes.name: train_roster
nodes.summary: Top-level entry point that optionally regenerates observation data for a cohort and then trains every student in a roster sequentially, tracking progress with a rich progress bar.

nodes.name: train_student
nodes.summary: Trains a single student's policy network end-to-end: sets up optimizer and loss, optionally resumes from a checkpoint, loops over epochs computing train/test losses per data split, saves periodic and final checkpoints, runs mid-training flight deployment evaluations, and selects the best checkpoint based on evaluation loss.

nodes.name: get_network
nodes.summary: Retrieves a named sub-network from a Policy object and sets it to training mode, returning the network along with the list of parameters to optimize.

nodes.name: observation_generator.py
nodes.summary: Generates neural-network training observations by replaying recorded flight rollout and image data through a Pilot's ORCA control loop with randomized noise injection, then compresses and saves the resulting input/output tensors per pilot network to disk.
nodes.languageNotes: Injects Gaussian position/velocity noise around ground-truth trajectories to synthesize a richer training distribution for imitation-learning-style policy supervision.

nodes.name: generate_observation_data
nodes.summary: Top-level entry point that iterates over a roster of pilots, loads each pilot's rollout and image course data, instantiates a Pilot, generates observations via generate_observations, and saves them via save_observations, reporting progress throughout.

nodes.name: generate_observations
nodes.summary: Replays a trajectory and image set through a Pilot's ORCA loop with injected positional/velocity noise, subsampling timesteps and extracting per-network input/output tensor pairs for training data.

nodes.name: save_observations
nodes.summary: Aggregates generated observation batches per network, builds a syllabus of keys, and writes each network's compiled input/output tensors to a .pt file under the cohort's observation_data directory.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Top-level project readme for SousVide (Scene Understanding via Synthesized Visual Inertial Data from Experts), covering installation steps (submodules, ACADOS build, conda environment, GSplat download) and pointing users to the notebooks/ folder for FiGS and SousVide usage examples.

nodes.name: environment_x86.yml
nodes.summary: Conda environment specification (env name 'kitchen') pinning Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.1.2 with CUDA 11.8, and pip-installed research dependencies including nerfstudio, tiny-cuda-nn, and editable installs of the local FiGS and sousvide packages.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses conda's mixed conda/pip dependency blocks plus git and local editable (`-e`) pip installs for submodule packages (FiGS, acados_template, Hierarchical-Localization).

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Python packaging configuration (setuptools build-backend) defining the 'sousvide' package, version 0.1.0, requiring Python >=3.10 with core scientific/ML dependencies (numpy, scipy, qpsolvers, albumentations, torch, torchvision, nerfstudio), and locating packages under src/.

nodes.name: default.json
nodes.summary: Default capture configuration template with no camera intrinsics set, specifying image extraction settings (300 images, 20 marked, ArUco marker length/id) used as a fallback when generating training data from real-world video captures for GSplat reconstruction.

nodes.name: iphone15pro.json
nodes.summary: Capture device configuration for an iPhone 15 Pro, providing OpenCV camera intrinsics (focal lengths, principal point, distortion coefficients) at 1920x1080 resolution plus the same image-extraction settings as the default profile, used when processing device-recorded video into GSplat training data.

nodes.name: pixel8pro.json
nodes.summary: Capture device configuration for a Google Pixel 8 Pro, providing OpenCV camera intrinsics (focal lengths, principal point, distortion coefficients) at 1920x1080 resolution plus the same image-extraction settings as the default profile, used when processing device-recorded video into GSplat training data.

nodes.name: button_prod.json
nodes.summary: Drone flight course definition for a short 'button' production trajectory, specifying 3 timed keyframes of flat-output states (position, yaw, and derivatives) over about 4 seconds with no external force profile.
nodes.languageNotes: Each keyframe's 'fo' matrix holds per-derivative flat-output values (rows likely x, y, z/altitude, yaw; columns are derivative order), consistent with differentially-flat quadrotor trajectory generation; 'Nco' likely sets the polynomial/spline coefficient count used by the trajectory optimizer that consumes this file.

nodes.name: circuit.json
nodes.summary: Drone flight course definition for a 'circuit' loop trajectory, specifying 10 timed keyframes of flat-output states spanning roughly 12 seconds with no external force profile.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest of the four course files, with denser keyframing (sub-second spacing at points) to capture sharper turns along the circuit path.

nodes.name: infinity.json
nodes.summary: Drone flight course definition for a figure-eight ('infinity') trajectory, specifying 7 timed keyframes of flat-output states spanning roughly 12 seconds with no external force profile.

nodes.name: traverse.json
nodes.summary: Drone flight course definition for a 'traverse' trajectory, specifying 6 timed keyframes of flat-output states spanning roughly 14 seconds with no external force profile.

nodes.name: data_alpha.json
nodes.summary: Lightweight data-generation method config for the synthesize pipeline: 3 short (2s) rollouts at 3Hz under mild domain randomization, with no injected model or sensor noise. Represents the smallest/fastest tier of a data-generation series (alpha/beta/gamma) likely used for quick smoke-testing of trajectory synthesis.

nodes.name: data_beta.json
nodes.summary: Medium-scale data-generation method config: 10 rollouts of 2s duration at 10Hz under the same domain-randomization ranges as data_alpha, with no injected noise. The middle tier of the alpha/beta/gamma data-generation progression.

nodes.name: data_gamma.json
nodes.summary: Largest-scale data-generation method config: 20 rollouts of 3s duration at 10Hz with the same domain-randomization ranges as alpha/beta, producing the most extensive training dataset in the alpha/beta/gamma progression.

nodes.name: eval_challenged.json
nodes.summary: Evaluation method config for a 'challenged' scenario: 10 rollouts with wider initial-condition randomization than the nominal case plus injected sensor noise (large position/attitude std) and no model noise, used to stress-test a trained policy under perturbed starting conditions and noisy measurements.

nodes.name: eval_extreme.json
nodes.summary: Most demanding evaluation method config: combines wide initial-condition randomization with both model (process) noise and sensor noise at the largest magnitudes of the eval_* set, used to test worst-case policy robustness.
nodes.languageNotes: The 10-element mean/std arrays for model and sensor noise likely correspond to per-channel noise on a drone state vector (e.g., position, attitude, and rate/velocity terms), scaled independently for each channel.

nodes.name: eval_mocap.json
nodes.summary: Evaluation method config modeling realistic motion-capture sensor noise: 10 rollouts with wide initial-condition randomization and small, hardware-realistic sensor noise standard deviations (no model noise), used to evaluate a policy under conditions approximating a real mocap-equipped test rig.

nodes.name: eval_nominal.json
nodes.summary: Baseline evaluation method config: 10 rollouts under the same mild domain-randomization ranges used for data generation, with no injected model or sensor noise, serving as the nominal/clean-condition benchmark against which challenged, extreme, and mocap evaluations are compared.

nodes.name: eval_single.json
nodes.summary: Minimal evaluation method config for a single deterministic rollout: randomization ranges and initial-condition perturbation are zeroed out and no noise is injected, used for debugging or visualizing one clean trajectory rather than statistical evaluation.

nodes.name: basic.json
nodes.summary: Defines the field-name schema for the 'basic' neural network I/O modality, listing named channels for vehicle state (current pose/velocity/orientation), control command, physical parameters, wrench, resultant force/torque, and placeholder slots for feature vectors and class tokens.
nodes.languageNotes: Each top-level key maps to a list of per-dimension labels (or null placeholders for unnamed tensor dimensions like feature_vector/class_token), used to auto-generate normalization and indexing logic for network inputs/outputs.

nodes.name: image.json
nodes.summary: Defines the field-name schema for the 'image' neural network I/O modality, specifying spatial (null) dimensions plus named channel labels for rgb_image, depth_image, feature_array, and patches tensors.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses null entries to represent unlabeled spatial (height/width) dimensions of image-like tensors, with only the channel dimension explicitly named (e.g. r/g/b, d).

nodes.name: sequence.json
nodes.summary: Defines the field-name schema for the 'sequence' neural network I/O modality, describing time-series inputs/outputs such as dynamics (dt, pose, velocity, orientation, thrust/torque command), wrenches, feature_arrays, and fo_horizon (flat-output horizon) trajectories.
nodes.languageNotes: Each key's outer null entry represents the time-step dimension, followed by the named per-timestep feature labels, consistent with sequence-model (e.g. transformer/RNN) input framing.

nodes.name: Iceman.json
nodes.summary: Pilot configuration for the 'Iceman' learned flight policy: defines a two-stage network architecture (a SIFU-style histNet that predicts dynamics parameters from state history, feeding an SVNet-style commNet that maps RGB images plus quaternion state to body-rate/thrust commands) running at 20 Hz, plus additive data-augmentation noise settings for training.
nodes.languageNotes: Layered JSON schema mirrors the sousvide Pilot's two-network design: a history/dynamics estimator (histNet) whose output feature vector conditions a vision-conditioned command network (commNet).

nodes.name: Jester.json
nodes.summary: Pilot configuration for the classical 'Jester' MPC-based policy, specifying trajectory planning (time-cost weight kT) and a 20 Hz tracking controller with state/input cost weights (Qk, Rk, QN), slack weights (Ws), and input bounds — no neural network is used.

nodes.name: Maverick.json
nodes.summary: Pilot configuration for the 'Maverick' learned flight policy, extending the Iceman-style histNet/commNet architecture with additional altitude and velocity terms (pz, vx, vy, vz) in the dynamics and vision-conditioning inputs, running at 20 Hz with the same additive data-augmentation settings.
nodes.languageNotes: Richer state vector (adds pz, vx, vy, vz) compared to Iceman.json, suggesting a policy variant trained with fuller state observability.

nodes.name: Rooster.json
nodes.summary: Pilot configuration for the 'Rooster' learned flight policy: pairs a SIFU histNet dynamics estimator with a DINO-based vision feature extractor (featNet) and a plain dnnet command head (commNet) that consumes DINO patch/class-token features plus the estimated feature vector to produce flight commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a pretrained DINO backbone (featNet) as a frozen/foundation feature extractor rather than the custom SVNet used by Iceman/Maverick, reflecting a scene-understanding-focused pilot variant central to the project's SUSVIED approach.

nodes.name: Viper.json
nodes.summary: Pilot configuration for the classical 'Viper' MPC-based policy, mirroring Jester.json's plan/track structure with slightly different orientation cost weights (Qk) for the 20 Hz tracking controller.

nodes.name: .gitmodules
nodes.summary: Git submodule manifest that registers the external FiGS simulator repository (github.com/StanfordMSL/FiGS.git) as a submodule of the SousVide project.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Ignore-pattern configuration for the Understand-Anything analysis tool, listing gitignore-style globs (build artifacts, generated code, test data, pretrained models) that can be excluded from codebase scanning.

nodes.name: carl.json
nodes.summary: Drone frame configuration defining the 'carl' vehicle's physical parameters (mass, inertia, rotor arm lengths, motor coefficients) and onboard camera intrinsics/extrinsics used by the FiGS simulator and flight stack.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Static project landing page for the SOUS VIDE paper, presenting the abstract, FiGS/SV-Net figures, deployment videos, and BibTeX citation, built on the Bulma CSS framework.

nodes.name: bulma.css.map.txt
nodes.summary: Empty placeholder text file accompanying the vendored Bulma CSS source map, containing no analyzable content.

nodes.name: index.css
nodes.summary: Custom stylesheet for the SOUS VIDE project page overriding Bulma defaults for typography, the publication header, video embeds, the results carousel, and the interpolation image slider panel.

nodes.name: bulma-carousel.js
nodes.summary: Vendored, webpack-bundled third-party Bulma Carousel library providing the carousel/slideshow widget used to display result videos on the project landing page.
nodes.languageNotes: Babel/webpack-transpiled UMD bundle with ES5 class-emulation helpers (_classCallCheck, _inherits, _possibleConstructorReturn); not project-authored code.

nodes.name: bulma-slider.js
nodes.summary: Vendored, webpack-bundled third-party Bulma Slider library providing the range-slider widget used for the interpolation image viewer on the project page.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: Page-specific script for the project landing page that wires up the navbar burger menu, initializes the Bulma carousel and slider widgets, and preloads/animates the interpolation image sequence.

nodes.name: figs_examples.ipynb
nodes.summary: Example Jupyter notebook demonstrating the FiGS workflow: generating a Gaussian Splat environment from a video capture, running an MPC-expert-controlled drone trajectory through the simulator, and rendering the onboard camera view to video.

nodes.name: sous_vide_examples.ipynb
nodes.summary: Example Jupyter notebook walking through the full SOUS VIDE pipeline: generating rollout and observation data, training the histNet and commNet policy networks, and evaluating the trained policy in the FiGS simulator.

nodes.name: command_helper.py
nodes.summary: Low-level flight helper module providing RealSense camera setup/capture, drone state/command coordinate transforms, and MAVSDK/PX4 offboard-control message publishing functions used to fly the real drone.

nodes.name: get_camera
nodes.summary: Configures and starts a RealSense camera pipeline at the requested resolution/frame rate, enabling color and depth streams and disabling auto-exposure/white-balance for consistent onboard image capture.

nodes.name: get_image
nodes.summary: Waits for a frame set from the camera pipeline and returns the color and depth images as numpy arrays, falling back to blank frames if no frame is available.

nodes.name: close_camera
nodes.summary: Stops the given RealSense camera pipeline, releasing camera resources.

nodes.name: vo2x
nodes.summary: Transforms a raw visual-odometry state estimate into the drone's state vector via a coordinate frame transform and normalizes the orientation quaternion.

nodes.name: x_transform
nodes.summary: Applies a rigid-body coordinate frame transform to a state vector, rotating position, velocity, and orientation quaternion from one reference frame to another.

nodes.name: am2unf
nodes.summary: Converts a raw accelerometer/motor measurement array into the unit-normalized force representation used by the flight controller.

nodes.name: vrs2uvr
nodes.summary: Converts a vehicle-rate-setpoint array into the normalized unit vehicle-rate command representation.

nodes.name: publish_uvr_command
nodes.summary: Builds and publishes a VehicleRatesSetpoint message carrying body-rate and thrust commands to the flight controller over the vehicle-rate-setpoint publisher.

nodes.name: engage_offboard_control_mode
nodes.summary: Publishes a VehicleCommand message that switches the flight controller into PX4 offboard control mode.

nodes.name: land
nodes.summary: Publishes a VehicleCommand message that commands the drone to land.

nodes.name: heartbeat_offboard_control_mode
nodes.summary: Publishes a periodic OffboardControlMode heartbeat message required by PX4 to keep offboard body-rate control active.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: SousVide (Scene Understanding via Synthesized Visual Inertial Data from Experts) is a Stanford MSL research project for training and deploying learned drone flight-control policies. The README explains the pipeline at a high level: an expert controller flies trajectories inside a Gaussian-splat simulator (FiGS) to synthesize training data, a policy network is trained on that data, and the trained policy can then be deployed back into simulation or onto a real drone. It also covers setup: cloning the FiGS submodule, building the ACADOS MPC solver, and creating the 'kitchen' conda environment.

tour.title: Usage Walkthrough Notebook
tour.description: Since this is a research library rather than an application with a single entry point, the sous_vide_examples notebook is the practical starting point for understanding how the pieces connect. It walks through generating rollout and observation data, training the histNet/commNet policy networks, and evaluating the trained policy in FiGS simulation end to end. Keep this notebook in mind as a map -- every module explored in the rest of this tour plugs into one of its steps.

tour.title: Pilot and Network I/O Configuration
tour.description: Nearly everything in SousVide is parameterized by JSON configs rather than hardcoded. A pilot config like Iceman.json declares a full two-stage network architecture (a SIFU history-encoder feeding an SVNet command network) purely as data, while the nnio schemas (basic.json, sequence.json) define the named tensor channels -- state, image, command, feature vectors -- that every network architecture reads and writes. Understanding this config vocabulary first makes the code in later steps much easier to follow, since the code is largely generic dispatch logic driven by these declarations.

tour.title: Vehicle Frame and Flight Courses
tour.description: Two more config families complete the parameterization picture: frame configs like carl.json define a physical drone's mass, inertia, rotor geometry, and camera intrinsics/extrinsics, while course configs like circuit.json define timed keyframe trajectories (position, yaw, and derivatives) that an expert controller will fly. Together with the pilot and nnio configs from Step 3, these fully specify what vehicle flies, what path it flies, and what network processes its data -- all without touching Python code.

tour.title: Generating Synthetic Flight Data
tour.description: With configs in hand, the synthesize layer is where the pipeline actually begins: rollout_generator.py simulates an expert VehicleRateMPC controller flying perturbed frames and trajectories through the FiGS Gaussian-splat scene, producing raw flight trajectories and camera images. synthesize_helper.py supplies the pure helper functions behind this -- randomized frame sampling, initial-state perturbation, and trajectory batching -- while data_compress_helper.py compresses the resulting image stacks to JPEG bytes so datasets stay manageable on disk. This is the 'expert demonstration' half of the learning-from-demonstration approach the paper's name describes.

tour.title: Neural Network Foundation
tour.description: Before looking at any specific architecture, it helps to see the shared scaffolding all of them build on. base_net.py defines BaseNet, an abstract PyTorch nn.Module that every SousVide network subclasses to normalize its input/output configuration (the nnio schemas from Step 3) into index maps. network_helper.py provides the shared tensor-shape and positional-encoding utilities every architecture needs, and network_factory.py is the dispatcher: given a config dict, it instantiates the right network class by name and caches the result to disk. This trio has the highest fan-in in the codebase, meaning almost every other control-layer file depends on it.
tour.languageLesson: PyTorch models are typically built as nn.Module subclasses. BaseNet demonstrates the abstract-base-class pattern: it implements shared behavior (config normalization, dimension helpers) once, and concrete subclasses only need to implement their own forward() logic.

tour.title: Specialized Network Architectures
tour.description: Building on BaseNet, the individual architecture files each implement one strategy for turning sensor observations into flight commands: SVNet fuses a SqueezeNet image backbone with MLP branches over state and history; SIFU maps history sequences to estimated physical parameters (or a feature vector at deployment); Pave adds actor/critic heads for stochastic control; feature_extractors.py wraps a pretrained DINOv2 vision transformer; and DNNet fuses image, heatmap, and history features through a simpler MLP head. The pilot configs from Step 3 (Iceman, Rooster, Maverick) each mix and match these building blocks by name via network_factory.

tour.title: Assembling and Running the Policy
tour.description: Policy and Pilot sit on top of the individual network architectures. policy.py's Policy class chains multiple sub-networks built by network_factory (for example a featNet feeding a commNet) into one forward pass. pilot.py's Pilot class wraps a Policy inside an OODA-style control loop (Observe-Retain-Collate-Act), maintaining rolling history buffers and feeding live state, image, and force/torque observations through the network to produce control commands. This is the runtime object that both the data-synthesis pipeline and the real/simulated flight code drive.

tour.title: From Raw Rollouts to Training Tensors
tour.description: observation_generator.py closes the loop between synthesis and training: it replays the raw rollout and image data from Step 5 through a Pilot's ORCA control loop (Step 8) with randomized noise injection, then compresses and saves the resulting input/output tensors per network. This is the step that turns 'expert flew this trajectory' into 'here are labeled (input, output) pairs a network can learn from' -- the highest fan-out file in the synthesize layer.

tour.title: Training the Policy Network
tour.description: The instruct layer consumes the observation tensors from Step 9. synthesized_data.py's ObservationData Dataset wraps them for PyTorch's DataLoader; losses.py defines the LossFn class (summed MSE across prediction/label keys) plus mixture-of-experts regularizers; and train_policy.py -- the file with the highest fan-out in the whole codebase -- orchestrates the full training loop: regenerating data if needed, per-student training with checkpointing, periodic in-training evaluation via deploy_figs, and best-checkpoint selection.

tour.title: Deploying to Simulation and Real Drones
tour.description: The flight layer is where a trained Pilot (Step 8) actually flies. deploy_figs.py orchestrates roster-level closed-loop deployment in the FiGS simulator across configuration/course/pilot combinations, computing metrics and saving videos -- it's also what train_policy.py calls for in-training evaluation. flight_helper.py computes tracking-error and inference-time metrics from the resulting rollouts, while command_helper.py is the real-hardware counterpart, handling RealSense camera capture and MAVSDK/PX4 offboard control messages for flying an actual drone -- the 'coming soon' real-world deployment path mentioned in the README.

tour.title: Shared Utilities and Visualization
tour.description: Cutting across every layer above is a set of shared support tools. rich_utilities.py -- the second-highest fan-in file in the project -- provides the console progress bars and result tables used during both data generation (Step 5) and training (Step 10). plot_learning.py visualizes training loss curves and deployment results, and record_flight.py's FlightRecorder captures state, input, and camera images at each simulation timestep and renders them to video, which is what deploy_figs.py relies on to produce its output videos.

tour.title: Public Website and Build Environment
tour.description: Two supporting concerns round out the project. docs/index.html is the public GitHub Pages landing page for the SOUS VIDE paper, presenting the abstract, figures, and deployment videos referenced above. environment_x86.yml, pyproject.toml, and .gitmodules define how to actually build the project: the conda environment pins Python 3.10 and PyTorch with CUDA 11.8, pyproject.toml packages the 'sousvide' module under src/, and .gitmodules wires in the FiGS simulator submodule that every step in this tour ultimately depends on.
tour.languageLesson: pyproject.toml is the modern, PEP 517/518-standard way to declare a Python package's build backend and dependencies in one file, replacing the older setup.py. Combined with an environment.yml for conda-managed native/GPU dependencies (like CUDA-linked PyTorch), this is a common pattern for research code that mixes pure-Python packaging with heavy compiled dependencies.
